strategy_updates.business_unit: Canadian Banking – Retail Deposits & Day-to-Day Banking
strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Building a deposit-rate and fee pricing function that uses testing to protect margin and grow non-interest revenue
strategy_updates.current_model: Posted GIC rate grid by term and type (cashable, non-redeemable, market-linked, $500 minimum) plus account packages with monthly fees, rebates and transaction fees; exception pricing is handled through a deposits exception pricing desk.
posting_evidence: Two Toronto Senior Manager roles posted 2026-10-09: Pricing Strategy & Optimization (req 276112) and Day to Day Banking Fee Optimization (req 276125)
Deposit role leads the pricing meeting, carries out approved rate changes and runs pricing pilots, A/B tests and controlled rollouts; supports the Director, Pricing, Portfolio Management and ADS
Fee role owns a fee-optimization roadmap (fee structures, transaction fees, account packages, service charges, waivers) to grow non-interest revenue, using elasticity analysis
Deposit role asks for evaluation of AI/ML for pricing analytics and forecasting; a separate Manager, Pricing & Portfolio Management role runs the exception pricing desk and SmartBot tool

news.summary: Scotiabank reported record Q3 2026 results; Canadian Banking earned $1,071M (up 12% year over year) on a fifth consecutive quarter of margin expansion and strong fee income growth, with ROE of 19.4%.

strategy_updates.interpretation: Inference: after five quarters of margin expansion, Scotiabank is trying to make deposit pricing and fee pricing repeatable, test-driven disciplines rather than periodic rate-sheet decisions. Hiring two senior pricing managers on the same day suggests it is building a team rather than backfilling. The deposit role is about protecting margin as rates move and competitors run GIC specials. The fee role points to non-interest revenue as a growth lever, so candidates should expect conduct and regulatory scrutiny of any fee increases.
open_questions: How much pricing authority does the pricing meeting have compared with Treasury and Finance on deposit rates?
Is the fee-optimization roadmap aimed at fee increases, repackaging accounts, or reducing waivers, and how are conduct and FCAC constraints handled?
What testing infrastructure exists today for rate and fee experiments?
strategy_updates.caveat: Interpretation rests on the postings and one earnings release; no deposit- or fee-specific pricing news from the last three months was read.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Repricing cash-management and operating-deposit relationships while modernizing billing
posting_evidence: Director, Revenue Management, Global Transaction Banking (req 273028), Toronto, posted 2026-09-08
Leads strategic pricing, repricing and revenue optimization across GTB products, including pricing approval for cash management products and operating deposits
Leads a billing and pricing transformation: target-state billing operating model, billing infrastructure modernization, billing standards and controls
People leader; requires 5+ years of management experience and an understanding of GTB product financials and P&L levers
strategy_updates.interpretation: Inference: GTB appears to be treating pricing as a revenue lever and fixing billing leakage at the same time. Pairing repricing with billing modernization usually means fee schedules and exceptions have drifted and are not enforced consistently in billing systems. The role is likely part commercial (approving and repricing client relationships) and part transformation lead (billing operating model), so change-management skills will matter as much as pricing analytics.
open_questions: Where does pricing approval authority sit today: relationship managers, product, or this team?
How much revenue leakage from unbilled or mis-billed services is believed to exist?
Does the mandate cover only Canada or GTB's Latin American footprint as well?
strategy_updates.caveat: Based on the posting alone; no GTB pricing news or published fee schedules were found.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Making commercial auto rate-making more sophisticated
posting_evidence: Manager, Actuarial Commercial Auto Pricing (job ID 10363), posted 2026-10-02, hybrid in Montreal and 13 other Canadian cities; $140,000–$160,000 estimated range
Leads pricing reviews for all commercial auto products 'with a focus on improving pricing sophistication' and recommends strategies that vary by product type and regulatory framework
Prepares regulatory rate filings, designs new pricing models and tools, and manages direct reports; the Director, Commercial Actuarial Pricing assigns special projects
Several other Wawanesa actuarial pricing roles are open at the same time (pricing modelling, Alberta auto pricing), alongside the tracked Director, Direct Venture Pricing role
strategy_updates.interpretation: Inference: Wawanesa is rebuilding its actuarial pricing capability across lines; the careers site shows a cluster of pricing-modelling and auto-pricing roles opened in September–October 2026. For commercial auto, 'pricing sophistication' usually means more rating variables and model-based segmentation, which suggests a shift from manual or legacy rating to model-driven rating. The role is technical and regulatory, closer to actuarial than to commercial pricing strategy.
open_questions: Is an actuarial designation effectively required despite being listed as an asset?
Which provinces' commercial auto filings are the priority, and how does the regulatory framework constrain rate changes?
strategy_updates.caveat: No company pricing news was found; the interpretation rests on this posting and the visible cluster of related openings.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Raising QuickBooks prices and bundling AI into tiers, while testing new models for AI agents
strategy_updates.current_model: QuickBooks Online (US pricing page, read 2026-10-14): Free $0 (1 user), Simple Start $38/mo, Essentials $85/mo (3 users), Plus $140/mo (5 users), Advanced $340/mo (25 users), each with a 50%-off-for-3-months promo; AI features are bundled by tier; ACH bill pay has a $0.50 overage fee beyond monthly allotments; payroll is an add-on.
posting_evidence: Principal, Monetization Strategy (job ID 22644), Mountain View or Atlanta; base $222,000–$300,500; no posting date shown
Owns pricing and packaging across QuickBooks, Payroll, Payments, Mailchimp and Intuit Intelligence: tiering, good/better/best design, price points, discount logic and guardrails
Explicit mandate to design and test subscription, consumption-based and outcome-based models for AI and platform capabilities
Analytical toolkit named: willingness-to-pay studies, elasticity, conjoint, A/B price tests, demand modelling; player-coach mentoring pricing analysts; 10+ years required

news.summary: Intuit reported fiscal 2026 results (revenue $21.4B, up 14%) and guided fiscal 2027 growth to 9–10%; online ARPC growth was 15% for fiscal 2026 against 3% growth in online paying customers, QuickBooks Free passed 20,000 customers, and the three-year growth target for Global Business Solutions was reset to 10–15%.
news.source: Trefis (analysis of Intuit's Q4 FY2026 results, published 2026-08-28)

news.summary: A third-party guide reports QuickBooks Online increases of about 17–25% effective May 1, 2026 and a further adjustment on August 1, 2026, with Payroll up about 20%; Intuit's own pricing page now shows higher list prices than the guide ($38/$85/$140/$340).

strategy_updates.interpretation: Intuit's growth now depends on price and mix rather than customer count: ARPC grew 15% while paying customers grew only 3%. That puts the price-increase strategy under pressure as growth guidance falls. Inference: this role is meant to find the next monetization lever beyond list-price increases, namely consumption- or outcome-based pricing for AI agents, plus a Free tier funnel that converts to paid. Expect scrutiny of churn and of the price-value story, since Intuit already concedes it lost price-sensitive TurboTax customers to cheaper rivals.
open_questions: Will AI agent capabilities be metered separately or kept inside tier bundles?
How is churn after the 2026 QuickBooks increases being measured, and does it constrain further increases?
How does this role divide work with the existing Global Business Solutions pricing team?
strategy_updates.caveat: Price-increase history comes from a third-party blog whose figures conflict with Intuit's current page; Intuit's own call transcript was not read.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Moving from per-seat incident management to a platform fee plus credits
strategy_updates.current_model: Per its pricing page (read 2026-10-14): PD Reliability Platform tiers with an annual platform fee and bundled seats, events and AI actions: Starter $2,800/yr (10 seats), Essential $12,000/yr (20 seats), Plus $48,000/yr (50 seats), Ultimate custom; extra usage via prepaid credit packs that expire annually. Legacy Incident Management: Free (5 users) and Professional at $21/user/month annual ($25 monthly); AIOps and Advance still sold as add-ons.
posting_evidence: Director of Pricing & Monetization, San Francisco hybrid (2 days a week in office), base $180,000–$303,600
Reports to the VP of Product Strategy & Growth inside Product Development; inherits a Pricing Analyst, a Pricing Manager (SKU migrations) and a Technical PM / Monetization Ops role
Mandate: packaging architecture, feature tiering and entitlements, SKU design and experiments, discount governance, the monetization platform roadmap, and migrating legacy customers to the new plans
Prefers experience of a transition to usage-based pricing and of scaling toward $1B+ ARR

news.summary: PagerDuty reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $124.4M (up 0.8%), ARR of $501M and dollar-based net retention of 98%, guided FY2027 revenue to $491.5–496.5M, and cited a recent restructuring and AI-agent product upgrades.

strategy_updates.interpretation: With revenue flat and net retention below 100%, PagerDuty is using packaging to restart expansion: moving seat-based customers onto a platform fee with bundled AI actions and credits. The posting confirms the migration of legacy customers is the main job and that the team must move 'from execution support to strategic'. Inference: the hire will be judged on migration uplift and on stopping seat contraction, under a new CEO and after a roughly 15% workforce reduction, so pricing decisions will be closely watched by leadership.
open_questions: What share of the base is already on the Reliability Platform, and is migration forced at renewal or optional?
How are AI actions and credits priced relative to seats, and how much overage revenue is expected?
Does the new leadership team want price realization or adoption-led expansion first?
strategy_updates.caveat: The earnings release does not discuss pricing; the link between packaging and net retention is inference.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Pricing and packaging a growing multi-product portfolio (payments, Billing, Tax, usage billing) as a coherent set
strategy_updates.current_model: Per its Canadian pricing page (read 2026-10-14): cards at 2.9% + CA$0.30 domestic, +0.8% international, +2% currency conversion; Billing pay-as-you-go 0.7% of billing volume or from CA$770/mo on contract; Tax Basic 0.5% per transaction; Connect from 0.25%; Metronome usage billing from US$0.04 per 1,000 events plus 0.8% of billing volume; IC+ and volume or multi-product discounts on custom pricing.
posting_evidence: Portfolio Pricing Strategist, US-Remote, first published 2026-05-04 and still listed (updated 2026-10-07); 5–7 years of experience
Pricing Strategy team sits in Product Marketing (department '6447 Product Pricing') and works with Product, Finance and Sales
Mandate: frameworks for how products are priced and packaged together, willingness-to-pay research, impact models for revenue, margin and user behaviour, internal pricing playbooks
Other pricing openings run in parallel: Pricing Strategist (SSF/NYC), Product Marketing Manager, Portfolio Pricing, Deal Pricing roles, Pricing Activation Specialist

news.summary: Stripe cut standard Australian domestic card fees from 1.70% to 1.65% (+A$0.30 online, +A$0.10 in person) from October 1, 2026, and will cut international card fees from 3.50% to 2.80% from April 1, 2027, passing on lower interchange caps set by the Reserve Bank of Australia (the support page gives no publication date).

strategy_updates.interpretation: Inference: Stripe is staffing portfolio-level pricing because its product set (payments, Billing, Tax, Connect and now Metronome usage billing) is sold increasingly as a bundle, and standalone list prices invite margin leakage through discounts. The number of parallel pricing and deal-pricing openings suggests a maturing pricing organization with separate tracks for list pricing, portfolio packaging and deal pricing. The Australian cut shows payments pricing still follows regulation, so the room for value-based pricing lies mainly in software products and bundles.
open_questions: Is portfolio pricing meant to drive multi-product discounts or to increase attach rates at list price?
How is Metronome being packaged alongside Stripe Billing?
What decision rights does Product Marketing's pricing team have relative to Deal Pricing and Finance?
strategy_updates.caveat: Pricing figures come from the Canadian page, not US pricing; only one pricing news item was read and it is regulation-driven.
